bulletins.title: Open Enrollment Health Insurance and Medicare Scams
bulletins.summary: Scammers exploit the Open Enrollment window for Medicare and the health insurance Marketplace through spoofed calls and deceptive search results. Callers impersonate official programs and press consumers to confirm policy details, verify Medicare numbers, or pay upfront registration fees.

bulletins.title: Urgent Bank Compromise and Emergency Impersonation Calls
bulletins.summary: Perpetrators reach targets via phone and SMS claiming an urgent security crisis, such as a compromised bank account or an emergency involving a loved one. Callers manufacture high urgency to pressure victims into transferring funds or handing over banking credentials before verifying facts independently.

bulletins.title: Fake Bank Investigator and Recovery Fee Schemes
bulletins.summary: Callers pose as bank fraud department representatives or regulatory recovery agents contacting previous fraud victims. They state that stolen money has been located or that an account is frozen, demanding advance payments for administrative fees, deposits, or taxes before funds can be restored.

gemini_context_snippet: Watch for incoming calls claiming a consumer's bank account has been compromised or demanding upfront fees to recover previously lost funds. Be alert to Open Enrollment health insurance callers seeking Medicare numbers and personal information under pressure.
